title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Company-wide canonical guidance that consolidates API design, coding conventions, infrastructure IaC practices, model-serving requirements, observability conventions, performance SLOs, and the ADR process. This page is the single landing reference for creating or reviewing standards and ADRs that affect runtime, APIs, and infra for inference services.
body:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single canonical reference for architecture and engineering standards that affect Redwood Inference runtime and platform services.
- Reduce divergence across teams in API design, code quality, infra, model-serving, observability, and performance work.

Scope
- Applies to hosted APIs, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Applies to services that implement inference (front-end request handling, routing, batching, model adapters, caching, and observability).
- Does not replace team-level design docs; teams must reference these standards when writing design PRDs and ADRs.

Owners and contact
- Standards owner: eng-architecture (rotating owners).
- Primary contact: aisha.patel@redwoodinference.com (architecture).
- Review cadence: quarterly review or when a breaking change is proposed.

1) API Standards\nIntro
- APIs must be stable, discoverable, and instrumented. Design decisions should minimize breaking changes and support gradual rollouts.

Design principles
- Use RESTful resources for admin endpoints and HTTP/JSON for public-hosted endpoints. Internal/high-throughput connections may use gRPC.
- Keep payloads explicit and schema-driven; prefer OpenAPI for REST endpoints and Protocol Buffers for gRPC.
- Versioning: use semantic versioning for public API surface (e.g., /v1/..., /v2/...). Default to header-based negotiation only for advanced use cases.
- Backwards compatibility: non-breaking changes allowed (add optional fields). Breaking changes require an ADR and coordinated rollout.

Authentication and authorization
- All public endpoints require token auth (Bearer). Use RBAC claims in tokens and validate at the edge.
- For Private deployments, support customer-managed OIDC/KMS integration; document mapping in integration guide.

Error handling
- Use standard HTTP status codes. Return error bodies with: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional array}.
- Transient errors (5xx) should include retryable hint and recommended backoff.

Schema & sample OpenAPI fragment
- Provide a short OpenAPI example for generation endpoint:

  "paths": {
    "/v1/generate": {
      "post": {
        "summary": "Generate text from model",
        "requestBody": {
          "content": {
            "application/json": {
              "schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "model": {"type": "string"},
                  "prompt": {"type": "string"},
                  "max_tokens": {"type": "integer"}
                },
                "required": ["model", "prompt"]
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "responses": {
          "200": {"description": "Successful response"},
          "400": {"description": "Bad request"},
          "429": {"description": "Rate limited"},
          "500": {"description": "Server error"}
        }
      }
    }
  }

Pagination and streaming
- For list endpoints use cursor-based pagination.
- For large generation responses prefer HTTP streaming with chunked transfer for hosted API. Document the streaming contract in the OpenAPI extensions.

Rate limiting and quotas
- Implement per-token and per-route quotas. Client libraries should surface 429 with quota metadata headers: X-Quota-Limit, X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Reset.

2) Coding standards

Languages and frameworks
- Backend services: Go for latency-critical components and core runtime; Python for evaluation and orchestration tooling where developer velocity is prioritized.
- Frontend/console: TypeScript + React.

Conventions
- Follow canonical styleguides: gofmt/goimports for Go, black/isort/flake8 for Python, ESLint/Prettier for TypeScript.
- Prefer small pure functions, explicit interfaces, and dependency injection for testability.

Testing and quality
- Unit tests: target >= 80% coverage for critical runtime packages.
- Integration tests: every PR touching runtime or model adapters must include integration tests against the benchmarking harness (see runtime benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
- Fuzzing for parsers, schema validation, and tokenizers where applicable.

CI/CD requirements
- Lint and static analysis must pass before merge.
- PRs must be reviewed by at least one owner in the affected subsystem.
- Merge gating: green build + 1 approver + security scan for code that handles user data.

PR guidance
- Keep PRs < 400 lines when possible. For larger changes include a design summary and a link to the ADR.

3) Infrastructure standards (IaC)

Principles
- All cloud resources must be provisioned via Terraform modules housed in the org repo. Ad-hoc console changes must be captured in IaC and reconciled within 24 hours.

Module conventions and naming
- Use shared modules for common patterns (networking, compute, k8s clusters, storage, kms).
- Naming convention: <env>-<stack>-<service>-<resource> (e.g., prod-inference-gateway-nlb).

Secrets and keys
- Use customer-managed KMS where available. Secrets must be stored in the secrets manager and consumed via short-lived credentials. No plaintext secrets in repo.

Networking and segmentation
- Production tenant networks: private subnets for compute, NAT/egress policies with centralized egress filtering, and VPC peering for Private deployments per reference-architectures.

Capacity and scheduling
- GPU fleet capacity planning: maintain 7-day and 30-day forecasts in eng-sre/capacity-planning. Define headroom policy of 20% reserved for burst and failover.

4) Model-serving standards

Model packaging and artifacts
- Models must be stored in an immutable artifact registry (S3 + manifest). Each artifact includes model weights, config, tokenizer, and a manifest.json with schema: { model_name, version, commit_sha, quantization_profile }.

Versioning and rollouts
- Semantic model versions (major.minor.patch). Model rollouts require: smoke tests, canary traffic (5% for 24 hours), quality regression checks against the evaluation prompt set, and automatic rollback on quality regressions or infra errors.

Quantization and profiles
- Quantization profiles are part of the manifest and describe supported backends (fp16, int8, ngquant). Runtime will select kernels based on profile and hardware.

Serving runtime requirements
- Support KV cache warmup and continuous batching. Provide hooks for model-specific optimizations (custom kernels).
- Fallback policy: if model error/routing failure occurs, fallback to a compatible model variant annotated in the model manifest.

Security and data handling
- No model artifacts should include customer PII. For fine-tuning or RLHF artifacts containing customer data, follow secure-sdlc and mark artifacts as restricted.

5) Observability standards

Metrics
- Metric names must follow the metric namespace: redwood.<service>.<component>.<metric>. Use Prometheus exposition format.
- Required service-level metrics:
  - redwood.<service>.requests_total (counter)
  - redwood.<service>.requests_errors_total (counter, labeled by error_type)
  - redwood.<service>.request_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - redwood.<service>.tokens_consumed_total (counter)
  - redwood.<service>.model_cache_hit_ratio (gauge)

Tracing and logs
- Traces: instrument per-request trace id propagated through gateway -> router -> runtime -> model adapter. Use OpenTelemetry.
- Logs: structured JSON logs at info/error levels. Sensitive fields must be redacted before logging.

Dashboards and alerts
- Each service must provide: a health dashboard (errors, latency p50/p95/p99, throughput), capacity dashboard (utilization, queue depth), and model-quality dashboard (eval pass rates, regression alerts).
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - SLO error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes -> P0 notification.
  - p99 latency breach > 2x SLO for 5 minutes -> paging.

SLOs and burn rate
- Define SLOs per public-facing route: availability and latency SLOs. Track error budgets and run burn-rate playbooks in eng-sre/runbooks.

6) Performance standards

Latency and throughput targets
- Default SLOs for inference endpoints (hosted API):
  - p50 <= 50ms, p90 <= 150ms, p99 <= 500ms (for short-context requests; high-context/long-generation endpoints have separate profiles).
  - Throughput: capacity measured in tokens/sec per GPU and per shard; teams must publish tokens/sec baselines for each model variant.

Performance testing
- All runtime changes must be validated against the benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Benchmarks include cold-start, steady-state, kv-cache-warm, and mixed workload scenarios.

Optimization guidance
- Use batching and KV caching heuristics recommended by Redwood Optimize. Record benchmark results in a standardized CSV: columns = [model, hardware, batch_size, seq_len, tokens_per_sec, p50, p95, notes].

7) Decision records (ADRs)

When to write an ADR
- An ADR is required when proposing an architectural change that is cross-team, affects public APIs, changes infra patterns, or changes SLOs/SLAs.

ADR template (short)
1. Title
2. Status (proposed/accepted/deprecated)
3. Context and Problem Statement
4. Considered Options (pros/cons)
5. Decision (what and why)
6. Consequences and Migration Plan
7. Owner and Reviewers

Example ADR summary
- ADR 2026-01: Continuous batching as default for model runtime
  - Status: accepted
  - Decision: Enable continuous batching in the serving runtime by default for production pools, with per-customer opt-out via config.
  - Rationale: Reduces per-token cost and improves overall throughput for mixed workloads while maintaining tail latency targets with adaptive batching.
  - Consequences: Requires changes to batching scheduler, additional metrics for batch composition, and a migration window for latency-sensitive customers.

Process and storage
- ADRs must be authored in the architecture repo under directory: docs/adrs and referenced from Confluence. Each ADR must include a review list and an implementation owner.

8) Compliance and exception handling

- Exceptions to these standards require a documented risk assessment and manager-level approval. Store exception records in security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions.

9) Governance and change process

- Proposals: create a Confluence design doc that references affected sections and an ADR if applicable.
- Review: architecture review board (weekly) evaluates changes that affect multiple teams.
- Rollout: adopt phased rollout with canaries and monitoring; create a rollback plan before production traffic is increased.

Appendix: Quick reference and snippets

Terraform naming example
- module "inference_gateway" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/modules.git//networking/gateway"
    name   = "prod-inference-gateway"
  }

OpenTelemetry snippet (Go)
- // Initialize tracer provider
  tp := otel.GetTracerProvider()
  ctx, span := tp.Tracer("gateway").Start(ctx, "handleRequest")
  defer span.End()

ADR checklist for authors
- State the problem and include quantitative impact where possible.
- List alternatives considered and non-functional implications (cost, latency, security).
- Identify migration and rollback steps.
- Add reviewers from impacted teams: runtime, infra, eng-sre, product.

Related references
- architecture-standards-api-coding-infra-model-serving-observability-performance-2026-03-04.json
- runtime-architecture/README and benchmarking-and-perf-suite pages.

Conformance
- Teams should include a short conformance note in PR descriptions when changes touch standards (e.g., "Conforms to architecture standards v2026-02").

Revision history
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-02-20: Added ADR process and updated performance targets (reviewers: Miguel Santos, Claire Huang).

If you have questions or want a working session to adopt any of these details, contact eng-architecture or open a PR to the architecture repo.
